claim: Under high RF-power conditions, the conversion of Si-H to Si-OH becomes more efficient, but if the temperature is insufficient, Si-OH groups can be buried before undergoing condensation, leading to incomplete densification and higher hydrogen content.
falsifier: The trade-off can be tested by depositing films at various combinations of RF power and temperature and measuring film density and hydrogen content, then identifying conditions where Si-OH burial occurs.

conditions: Deposition is performed using PECVD with silane and oxygen precursors
RF power is high enough to enhance Si-H to Si-OH conversion
Temperature is below the threshold needed to activate condensation reactions before burial
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the simulated conditions and the specific precursor chemistry studied; transfer to other power and temperature ranges is unestablished.

title: High RF power combined–Incomplete condensation of Si-OH boundary
